headline: Lab-aged microplastics shown to bind copper in wastewater, altering environmental toxicity
text: Researchers at Baylor University simulated microplastic aging at wastewater treatment plants and found that microplastics actively bind copper, potentially altering how the metal moves through environments and increases its toxicity when discharged into natural waters. Both pristine and degraded microplastics attached to copper regardless of their condition, and the study shows wastewater plants are major pathways for plastic particles into natural waters. While the researchers caution that results under laboratory conditions may differ from real environmental behavior, they conclude that microplastics are not static contaminants.
